title: Baseball Through Data
text:
Baseball Through Data
This site explores a few of the big stories hidden in MLB history using the Lahman database. One page shows that the apparent home-run boom in short seasons is mostly an illusion once we measure home runs per game instead of raw totals, revealing that unusual seasons look much more ordinary when adjusted for season length. Another page highlights the career home run leaders and puts their totals in context across multiple eras.
The analysis pages are available in the navbar, so you can move between the season-by-season home run story and the player-level leaderboards to see the same data from different angles.
